title: Surveillance Company Tells Cops It Wants to Add Facial Recognition to Flock Cameras

agency_candidates.display_name: 1st Judicial District Drug Task Force TN (Inactive)
East Tennessee State University TN Campus PD

summary: Third-party surveillance company VIDIZMO is marketing to police the ability to ingest Flock ALPR and livestream camera data into its own platforms that perform facial recognition, behavior prediction, and race/gender/age classification, despite Flock's public pledge not to add facial recognition. A VIDIZMO salesperson pitched Johnson City, TN police on the integration; the department says it did not take the call. Critics say the pitch shows that once mass-surveillance infrastructure exists, other vendors will layer more invasive analytics on top.

key_quotes.quote: We will not add facial recognition to our devices

VIDIZMO Intelligence Hub closes that gap. It brings Flock Safety data, Axon body worn camera footage, and any other evidence source into one searchable platform. Investigators search across all of it simultaneously — by face, vehicle, or object in seconds.
An agency can import plate reads or clips that it has exported under its own authorized access. Flock has not been involved in or informed of this.
What Flock says about their capabilities is to some degree irrelevant because they have built the infrastructure for mass surveillance.
